plainTranslation: A's drive meets B's feelings. The square puts them in friction.
policy: Governed by synastry-policy. Descriptive, not deterministic; intensity is never treated as obligation, safety concerns override astrology.
note: Synced from authored synastry bundle synastry-authored__19_ (2).json.
summaryDeep: Their initiative, urgency, directness, and temper press against your feelings, needs, and sense of safety. It catches often enough that you both feel it, and it keeps asking to be worked out. Name it directly instead of letting it build in silence.
tension: The problem is when the friction becomes the main way you stay connected. If things only feel alive when someone is upset, the relationship can start to confuse tension with intimacy. You poke, they react. They push, you defend. After a while, both people are tired, but neither one knows how to get close without lighting something up first.
advice: Catch the small thing while it is still small. Not every feeling needs to become a fight. This connection works better when both people learn how to pause before trying to win the moment.
summaryShort: Their initiative, urgency, directness, and temper press against your feelings, needs, and sense of safety.
